scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Frug emerged in the mid-1960s as an evolution of the 'Chicken', a dance known for lateral body movements.
It gained popularity as a stationary alternative to the Twist, allowing dancers to maintain rhythm without constant foot movement.
It is closely related to other fad dances of the era like the Watusi and the Jerk.
on_screen: Map: USA · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Frug served as a social outlet for youth in the 1960s.
It represented a shift toward individualistic, non-partnered dancing and was often viewed as a symbol of the 'generation gap' between youth and their more conservative elders.
Today it is a revived tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers stand in place and move their hips vigorously from side to side.
The feet remain largely stationary while the torso and arms perform various expressive gestures.
It is a solo dance that emphasizes lateral motion and rhythmic intensity.
Watch for The Aloof, The Heavyweight.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (mcrZIK3gqbU)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Stationary solo dancing; requires very little floor space.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to mid-1960s pop and rock music.
The music typically features a strong 4/4 beat with a prominent backbeat, often provided by drums, electric guitars, and bass.
Listen for the Electric guitar, Drums, Bass guitar, Saxophone.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 120 beats a minute.
A driving mid-tempo rock or pop sound with a prominent snare drum backbeat and jangly electric guitars, typical of the 1964-1966 era.

narration: Typically performed in social settings like discotheques or parties. 1960s mod fashion, including miniskirts and boots, often accompanied the dance.
In theatrical contexts, it was performed in stylized, high-fashion costumes.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Bob Fosse is the most prominent figure associated with the dance, having choreographed 'The Rich Man's Frug' for the film Sweet Charity.
Norman Mailer also documented the dance in his cultural essays.
While primarily an American craze, the dance was known by several names including the Surf, Big Bea, and the Thunderbird.
The Frug descended from the Chicken and the Twist.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: The Frug is parent of The Chicken: The Frug evolved directly from the lateral body movements of the Chicken.
The Frug is sibling of The Twist: The Frug was used as a change-of-pace step for dancers doing the Twist.
The Frug is child of The Monkey: The Monkey is one of several arm-based variations that grew out of the Frug.

scenes.title: Try one step
narration: Before we go, one step. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Shift weight subtly between feet without lifting them from the floor.
Count it: 1-2-3-4 then 5-6-7-8 (eight counts, two bars).
Chapter 1 takes it slowly from here.

narration: Upright but relaxed, knees slightly soft to allow hip mobility.

narration: Count: 1-2-3-4 then 5-6-7-8 (eight counts, two bars). The meter is 4/4.

Clap it first, then step it in place.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Shift weight subtly between feet without lifting them from the floor.
Footwork from the sources: Stationary; feet stay planted on the floor.
Drill: Stand still and isolate hips side-to-side.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); repetitions per step: about 4
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Drive the hips laterally from left to right in time with the music.
Step 4: Keep the upper torso relatively loose to absorb the hip motion.
Drill: Match hip shifts to a 4/4 metronome.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Add a slight knee bounce to the hip rhythm.
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid excessive traveling; the essence of the Frug is staying in one spot.
